s.t: In the king's garden stood a tree of golden apples.
Every night, the thief took one golden apple from the tree.
Each morning, the king counted his golden apples.
One morning, an apple was gone.
The king called his three sons into the garden.
A thief takes an apple from my tree every night.
One of my sons must watch the tree tonight.

paras.summary: The king's golden tree loses an apple every night, so he calls his three sons and tells them to watch it.

s.t: Father, I am the eldest son.
I will watch the tree tonight.
Good.
Come and wake me if you see the thief.
Father, I will watch the tree too.
Tonight your brother will watch, and you will watch tomorrow.

paras.summary: The eldest son offers to watch first, and the king tells the second son he will watch the next night.

s.t: Night came, and the eldest son sat under the tree.
He watched the tree, and he waited for the thief.
He watched, but no thief came.
At midnight, he grew tired, and he fell asleep.
In the morning, another golden apple was gone.

paras.summary: The eldest son watches the tree, but at midnight he grows tired and falls asleep, and another apple is stolen.

s.t: You fell asleep, and the thief came again.
I am sorry, Father.
Father, let me watch the tree tonight.
Do not fall asleep like your brother.

paras.summary: The king scolds the eldest son for sleeping, and the second son asks for a turn to watch.

s.t: Night came again, and the second son sat under the tree.
He watched the tree, and he waited for the thief.
He watched, but no thief came.
Near midnight, he grew tired, and he fell asleep.
In the morning, another golden apple was gone.

paras.summary: The second son watches the tree, but near midnight he too grows tired and falls asleep.

s.t: Both of my elder sons have failed me, and I am worried.
Father, let me watch the tree tonight.
You will fail like your brothers.
Let him try.
He may do better than both of you.

paras.summary: Another apple is stolen, so the youngest son asks for a turn, and the king agrees to let him try.

s.t: That night, the youngest son sat under the golden tree.
He did not fall asleep this time.
He watched the tree closely, and he waited for the thief.
He watched, but no thief came.

paras.summary: The youngest son stays awake all night and watches the tree closely under the moon.

s.t: Near midnight, a golden bird came to the tree.
The bird took an apple from the tree.
The youngest son shot at the golden bird.
He only won one feather, and the bird flew away.
In the morning, the youngest son brought the feather to the king.

paras.summary: Near midnight, a golden bird comes to the tree, and the youngest son's shot only wins him one feather.

s.t: Father, I saw a golden bird take the apple.
I could not catch it, but here is a feather.
The king held the feather and looked at it closely.
I must have the golden bird.
My eldest son will go and find this golden bird.

paras.summary: He brings the feather to the king, who is amazed by it and sends the eldest son to find the bird.

chapterList.title: The Fox and the Two Brothers

s.t: The eldest son rode out to find the golden bird.
At the edge of a forest, a fox stepped onto the road.
Where are you going in a hurry?
I do not need your help, fox.
Listen to me, and I will help you.
Tonight you will find two inns in a village.
Stay at the poor inn, not the fine one.
I do not need advice from an animal.
The eldest son rode on and forgot the fox.

paras.summary: A fox meets the eldest son on the road and warns him to choose the poor inn, but he will not listen.

s.t: That night, he came to the village with two inns.
Loud music came from the fine inn.
The eldest son went inside and forgot his father's bird.
Days passed, and the eldest son did not come home.

paras.summary: The eldest son stays at the loud, merry inn and never returns home.

s.t: My eldest son has not come home.
My second son must go and find the bird now.
The second son rode out on the same forest road.
The same fox stepped onto the road before him.

paras.summary: The king sends the second son, and the same fox gives him the very same warning.

s.t: Stay at the poor inn, not the fine one.
I do not need advice from an animal.
The second son also went into the fine inn.
Days passed, and the second son forgot the golden bird too.

paras.summary: The second son also refuses to listen to the fox and is lost at the merry inn.

chapterList.title: The Youngest Son Meets the Fox

s.t: Both of my elder sons are gone.
Father, let me find the golden bird.
The youngest son rode out on the forest road.
The fox came onto the road before him.

paras.summary: The king is worried, and the youngest son rides out on the forest road to find the bird.

s.t: Where are you going in a hurry?
I look for a golden bird, fox.
I know where the golden bird is.
Fox, will you help me?
I will help you if you listen to me.
I promise to listen to you, fox.

paras.summary: The fox meets the youngest son, who promises to listen to it this time.

s.t: Tonight you will find two inns in a village.
Stay at the poor inn, not the fine one.
I will do as you say, fox.
That night, he came to the village.
Loud music came from the fine inn.
But the youngest son walked to the poor inn.
He slept at the poor inn that night.

paras.summary: The fox warns him about the two inns, and the youngest son obeys, choosing the poor one.

s.t: In the morning, the fox stood on the road.
Today you will come to a castle.
A golden bird sits in a wooden cage.
Take the bird, but take the wooden cage too.
Do not put the bird in the golden cage beside it.
I will take the wooden cage, fox.

paras.summary: The fox warns the youngest son to take the bird in its wooden cage, not the golden one.

s.t: The youngest son came to the castle that night.
He found the golden bird in its wooden cage.
A golden cage stood on the wall beside it.
He thought the bird looked poor in the plain cage.
He opened the golden cage and put the bird inside it.
The golden bird gave a loud cry.

paras.summary: At the castle, he finds the bird but puts it in the golden cage instead, against the fox's advice.

s.t: Guards ran into the castle and caught the youngest son.
Why did you try to steal my bird?
I wanted to bring it to my father.
I will spare your life for a promise.
Bring me the golden horse, and you may have the bird.
The youngest son agreed, and the guards let him go.

paras.summary: Guards catch him, and the Bird King spares his life if he brings back the golden horse.

s.t: The youngest son left the castle without the bird.
The fox stood on the road again.
You did not listen to me.
I am sorry, fox.
I will listen now.
I will forgive you and help you again.

paras.summary: The fox forgives the youngest son for disobeying and agrees to help him again.

s.t: Today you will come to a castle.
A golden horse stands with an old saddle.
Take the horse, but use the old saddle.
Do not put the golden saddle on the horse.
I will use the old saddle, fox.

paras.summary: The fox warns him to use the old saddle, not the golden one, at the next castle.

s.t: The youngest son came to the castle that night.
He found the golden horse in the castle.
A golden saddle stood on the wall.
He thought the horse looked poor in the old saddle.
He put the golden saddle on the horse.
The golden horse gave a loud cry.

paras.summary: He finds the golden horse but puts on the golden saddle instead, and the horse cries out.

s.t: Guards ran into the castle and caught the youngest son.
Why did you try to steal my horse?
I wanted the horse for my father.
I will spare your life for a promise.
Bring me the golden princess, and you may have the horse.
The youngest son agreed, and the guards let him go.

paras.summary: Guards catch him, and the Horse King spares his life if he brings back the golden princess.

s.t: The youngest son left the castle without the horse.
The fox stood on the road again.
You did not listen to me.
I am sorry, fox.
I will listen now.
I will forgive you and help you again.

paras.summary: The fox forgives the youngest son again and agrees to help him find the golden princess.

s.t: Tonight the golden princess will come to the garden.
Take her hand, and she will come with you.
Do not let her say goodbye to her father.
I will not let her say goodbye, fox.

paras.summary: The fox warns him not to let her say goodbye to her father before they leave.

s.t: That night, the youngest son took the princess's hand.
Where are you taking me?
I must bring you to a castle.
Let me say goodbye to my father.
The fox told me not to let you do that.
Her tears were enough, and he let her say goodbye.

paras.summary: He wins the princess's trust, but her tears convince him to let her say goodbye.

s.t: Her father woke and ran to the gate.
Guards ran out and caught the youngest son at the gate.
Why are you taking my daughter away?
I am sorry.
I only did what she asked.
You may have her if you pass one test.

paras.summary: Her father wakes and catches them, but offers one final test before she can go.

s.t: A hill stands outside my window.
Remove the hill in eight days, and you may take my daughter.
The youngest son looked at the hill, afraid.
He left by the gate, afraid and alone.
The fox stood outside the gate.

paras.summary: The Golden King demands the hill be removed in eight days, and the youngest son feels afraid.

s.t: Why do you look so afraid, my friend?
The king wants me to remove a hill.
Go and rest.
I will move the hill for you.
I cannot move a hill alone.
Trust me, and rest tonight.
The youngest son ate and fell asleep.

paras.summary: The fox promises to move the hill and tells him to rest and trust it.

s.t: That night, the fox called to foxes.
A thousand foxes came and dug at the hill.
By morning, the hill was gone.

paras.summary: Through the night, the fox and other foxes dig away the hill before morning comes.

s.t: You have passed the test, as I promised.
Take my daughter.
The youngest son and the princess rode away.

paras.summary: The Golden King keeps his promise, and the youngest son rides away with the princess.

s.t: The fox rode along beside the princess and the youngest son.
We must visit the Horse King, as you promised him.
I promised him the princess for the golden horse.
I will become the princess for one day.
The fox spoke a strange word and turned into a princess.
The real princess hid in a quiet cave and waited.

paras.summary: The fox agrees to become the princess so the youngest son can keep his promise to the Horse King.

s.t: The youngest son brought the fox to the Horse King.
The Horse King looked closely, but he saw no trick.
You kept your promise, so take the golden horse.
The youngest son rode away on the golden horse.
That night, the fox changed back and found the princess.

paras.summary: He trades the fox for the horse, and the fox later escapes and finds the real princess again.

s.t: Now we must visit the Bird King, as you promised him.
I promised him the horse for the golden bird.
This time, I will become the golden horse.
The real horse stayed safe near the princess.
The fox spoke a strange word and turned into a horse.

paras.summary: The fox then agrees to become the golden horse, and the real horse stays safe nearby.

s.t: The youngest son brought the fox to the Bird King.
The Bird King checked the horse but noticed nothing wrong.
You kept your promise, so take the golden bird.
That night, the fox slipped past the guards and ran.
The fox changed back into itself, safe in the forest.

paras.summary: He trades the fox for the bird, and the fox again slips away and changes back.

s.t: Fox, you have saved me three times now.
We are not finished yet, my friend.

paras.summary: The youngest son thanks the fox, who says their journey is not yet over.

s.t: The youngest son had the bird, the horse, and the princess.
They rode home.
Listen well now.
Do not pay to save a man.
And never sit at the edge of a well.
I will listen, fox.

paras.summary: The youngest son now has the bird, horse, and princess, and the fox gives one more warning.

s.t: On the road, men stood to kill two prisoners.
The youngest son looked and saw his brothers.
Do not kill these men.
I will pay for them.
He gave gold, and his brothers were free.
Thank you, brother.
We are sorry for what we did.
We should have listened to the fox.

paras.summary: He saves his own brothers from men about to kill them, against the fox's advice.

s.t: The youngest son let his brothers ride with him.
The brothers rode on and thanked him again.
That day, they came to a well.
Tired, the youngest son sat at the edge of the well.

paras.summary: The brothers travel on with him, and, tired, he sits at the edge of a well.

s.t: Our brother has the bird, the horse, and the princess.
Father will love him more than us.
We can take them for ourselves.
The youngest son rested, and his brothers came near him.
They pushed him into the well.
The youngest son fell into the water.

paras.summary: The jealous brothers push the youngest son into a well while he rests, planning to steal his prizes.

s.t: Now we will bring the bird, horse, and princess home.
We will tell Father that we won them.
Where is the man that saved me?
He stayed away.
He will not come home.

paras.summary: The brothers take the bird, horse, and princess, and plan to lie about what happened.

s.t: The princess did not believe the brothers.
I will not speak until he comes back.
The horse did not eat, and the bird did not sing.

paras.summary: The princess refuses to speak, and the horse and bird refuse to eat or sing without him.

s.t: The brothers brought the horse, bird, and princess to the king.
My sons are home!
Where is your brother?
He stayed away.
The king did not believe them.

paras.summary: The brothers bring the treasures home, but the king does not fully believe their story.

s.t: In the well, the youngest son called for help.
He called out, and the fox heard him.
I will save you.
The fox went to find help from the animals.
Animals came and pulled him out of the well.

paras.summary: The fox hears the youngest son and finds help from the forest animals to save him from the well.

s.t: Thank you, fox.
Your brothers pushed you in and took the bird, horse, and princess.
I cannot believe my brothers did this to me.
Now they have your bird, horse, and princess.

paras.summary: The fox tells him his brothers stole his prizes and lied to the king about him.

s.t: I must go home and tell the king the truth.
Do not go home like this.
Wear old clothes.
The princess, the horse, and the bird will know you.
They will not eat, sing, or speak until they see you.
I will go to my father's castle now.

paras.summary: The fox tells him to dress like a poor man, since the princess, horse, and bird will still know him.

s.t: The youngest son walked to his father's castle in old clothes.
The horse still did not eat.
The golden bird still did not sing.
The princess still did not speak.

paras.summary: The youngest son returns in old clothes, and the horse, bird, and princess still refuse to eat, sing, or speak.

s.t: The poor man walked into the castle.
The horse began to eat.
The bird began to sing.
That is him!
That is the man that saved me.

paras.summary: As soon as he enters the garden, the horse eats, the bird sings, and the princess knows him at once.

s.t: This poor man cannot be my youngest son.
The youngest son took off his old clothes.
The king saw his true son.
My son!
I believed you were lost.

paras.summary: He takes off his old clothes, and the king sees that his true son has returned.

s.t: My brothers pushed me into a well.
Is this true?
Both of you, come here now.
We wanted Father to be proud of us.
You lied to me.
You will both leave this castle and never return.
The two brothers walked out of the castle.

paras.summary: The truth of the brothers' betrayal comes out, and the king sends them away forever.

s.t: My son, you have won the golden bird and more.
Father, I want to marry the golden princess.
I want to marry him too, more than anything.
The king agreed, and the castle celebrated.

paras.summary: The king gives his blessing for the wedding, and the castle celebrates.

s.t: Fox, will you stay with us at the castle?
I have one more request before I can stay.
Ask me anything, fox.
I owe you my life.
Cut off my head, and then cut off my feet.

paras.summary: The fox asks for one final, strange request before it will agree to stay.

s.t: The youngest son was afraid.
I could never hurt you.
You have saved me.
You must trust me one more time, my friend.
I trusted you before.
It was right.
Trust me now, and do as I ask.

paras.summary: The youngest son refuses at first, but the fox asks him to trust it one last time.

s.t: The youngest son thought of all the fox had done.
You saved me from the well and moved the hill for me.
You helped me win the princess, and you saved me again.
I trust you, and I will trust you now.
He cut off the fox's head.
He cut off the fox's feet.

paras.summary: The youngest son remembers all the fox has done for him and finally does as it asked.

s.t: A golden light came into the garden.
Where the fox had stood, a young man stood now.
Brother!
I never thought to see you again.
A curse turned me into a fox.
Your true love could break the curse.

paras.summary: A golden light reveals a young man where the fox stood — the princess's own brother, freed from a curse.

s.t: Welcome to the castle, young man.
They all lived in peace.

paras.summary: The king welcomes the young man into the castle, and they all live in peace.
